wa_north_face_3.primary: Blue Lake Trail and the Concord-Lexington gully

why.Early-season snow to the Concord-Lexingt: Early season, from when the highway opens until late June, while the gully to the col still holds firm snow that buries the boot path; bring an axe, and crampons if it is refrozen.

wa_north_face_left_buttress.primary: Ross Lake boat crossing, Lightning Creek and the abandoned Freezeout Creek trail to the north-face glacier

why.Pacific Crest Trail north from Harts Pas: When no boat is available and you want to stay in the United States; it is about 27 miles each way along the crest from Harts Pass, which usually opens only in July.

wa_north_ridge_2.primary: From the west: Hannegan Pass, the Chilliwack River Trail and Brush Creek to Whatcom Pass

why.From the east: Ross Lake water taxi to L: When starting from the SR-20 side or linking a Pickets traverse out to Ross Lake; it skips the long Hannegan drive but needs a water taxi booked ahead from the resort.

wa_north_ridge_3.primary: The SR-20 South Buttress pullout, then bear right into the basin beneath the North Ridge Notch

why.Rainy Pass and Porcupine Creek into the: When camped near Rainy Pass or combining objectives; longer than the highway-side basin but simple to navigate, with cleaner rock and two or three short low-fifth pitches to the notch.

wa_north_ridge_west_side.primary: Rainy Pass, the PCT north and the ridge above Porcupine Creek

why.Cutthroat Lake and Cutthroat Pass: When starting from the Cutthroat Pass trailhead on the highway or combining with a Cutthroat Pass hike; it is mostly maintained trail, then about a mile of rotten ridge scrambling south from the pass.

why.Lyman Lakes basin to the south flank: When the Railroad Creek corridor is open again and you prefer the ferry and shuttle to crossing Spider Gap, whose glacier travel and steep climb it avoids.

wa_phantom_peak_south_route.primary: Hannegan Pass, Whatcom Pass and Perfect Pass to a camp on the Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine

why.Big Beaver Trail to Luna Camp, then the: When starting from SR-20 and wanting the shortest, flattest way into the Pickets; the water taxi and Big Beaver trail are easy, but the last stretch up Luna Creek is a pathless bushwhack.

wa_pinnacle_mountain_entiat_scramble.primary: North Fork Entiat over Saska Pass and Snow Brushy Creek

why.Entiat River trail and Snow Brushy Creek: When you want mostly maintained trail and reliable water at Snow Brushy Creek; it ends at Borealis Pass below the easy south slopes, though burned timber can hide the last faint trail.

wa_primus_peak_south_ridge.primary: The far end of the Eldorado ice cap: five glaciers and a notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col

why.Thunder Creek and the Borealis Glacier:: When you want a shorter two-day trip with fewer glaciers and fewer people; it costs a cold Thunder Creek crossing and brush, and it finishes on the east ridge, not this south side.

wa_prusik_peak_der_sportsman.primary: Aasgard Pass and the Core, fifty feet left of the standard south-face line

why.Snow Lakes and the lower Enchantments: Chosen to avoid the loose scree grind of Aasgard Pass; the Snow Lakes trail is longer but gentler and shaded on hot days, and it makes an easy walk out.
